analysis.one_liner: HDFC AMC runs HDFC Mutual Fund, earning fees as a percentage of the money it manages across equity, debt and other schemes.
analysis.whats_happening: HDFC AMC reported Q2 FY27 (quarter ended Sept 2026) results on October 15, 2026: consolidated PAT of Rs 749 crore, up just 4.2% year-on-year, while revenue from operations rose a healthier 14% to Rs 1,169 crore. Quarterly average AUM (QAAUM) reached Rs 9.69 lakh crore, up 10% YoY, with an 11.1% overall mutual fund market share and 12.7% share in actively managed equity funds. September SIP inflows hit a record Rs 32,500 crore.
analysis.plain_terms: The core business - managing money and collecting a fee on it - is growing well: AUM is up 10% and core operating profit from the asset management business rose 16% YoY. But the headline profit number looks weak because HDFC AMC also invests its own cash in markets, and the gains on that investment book fell sharply this quarter versus last. Strip that out and underlying profit grew closer to 12% YoY - the business is healthier than the 4% headline suggests, but a reader relying only on the headline would be misled.
analysis.quarters: Sequentially, PAT fell 10.5% - from Rs 837 crore in Q1 FY27 to Rs 749 crore in Q2 FY27 - even though revenue from operations rose 6.3% QoQ and EBITDA margin expanded to 79.65% (from 77.3%). The gap is explained by 'other income' (gains on the company's own investment book), which dropped from roughly Rs 263 crore in Q1 to Rs 71 crore in Q2 - a 26% YoY decline. This is not comparable to core fee income and should be read separately; operating profit from the core AM business grew a steady 16% YoY to about Rs 907 crore. Management flagged that softness in systematic flows is concentrated in STP (wealth-manager-driven transfers that pause when markets turn choppy), not in SIPs, where market share has actually risen.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 15.5% over one year and sits 16.8% below its August 2025 peak of Rs 2,883, though it has still returned 75% over 3 years and 82% over 5 years - both comfortably ahead of the Nifty (17% and 25% respectively) but far behind peer NAM-INDIA (200% and 176%). A 1:1 bonus issue (record date November 26, 2025) doubled the share count and roughly halved the nominal price; the return and drawdown figures here are already on a bonus-adjusted, comparable basis, so the 1-year and 3-month declines are genuine price moves, not a corporate-action artifact. The real story is relative: the market has rewarded NAM-INDIA's growth far more than HDFC AMC's over the past 1-3 years.
analysis.valuation_read: At a TTM P/E near 34x, the stock trades about 16% below its own 10-year median P/E of ~41x - so it is cheap relative to its own history, largely because growth has slowed and the stock has corrected from its peak. But it is NOT cheap in absolute terms: P/E is still roughly 15% above the asset-management peer median and well above the broader industry average, and P/B of about 10x is a 45% premium to the peer median of ~6.9x. The 'why it looks cheap' (self-comparison) and 'whether it is actually cheap' (peer/industry comparison) point in different directions - it is a quality business, but that quality is already priced in.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is both volume- and margin-led: QAAUM is up 10% YoY (volume), the equity AUM mix continues to rise giving a richer fee yield, and EBITDA margin expanded further to ~80% on operating leverage. Core operating profit grew 16% YoY, a cleaner read than the 4% headline PAT figure, which was dragged down by volatile non-core investment income.
analysis.health_read: Profits convert to cash easily - this is a fee-based, asset-light business with no borrowings (debt-to-equity of 0.00) and ROE near 36%, ROCE near 43%. There is effectively no financial risk here; the real risk is business/market risk - AUM and fee income are tied to equity market levels and investor sentiment, and the mutual fund industry periodically faces regulatory pressure on expense ratios (TER caps), which would compress fees industry-wide.
analysis.ownership_read: HDFC Bank is the controlling promoter with about 52.3-52.4% and has pledged none of its shares. The erstwhile co-promoter, Abrdn (formerly Standard Life), has fully exited its roughly 10% stake in stages over recent years and has ceased to be a co-sponsor of HDFC Mutual Fund - a structural change worth noting, not a red flag by itself. FIIs hold about 24% and DIIs about 14.5%, with large holders being institutional/index-type investors (e.g., Norway's sovereign fund, ICICI Pru MF, SBI MF, JPMorgan EM funds). There is no well-known individual investor on the shareholder register.
strengths: Zero debt with ROE ~36% and ROCE ~43% - a highly capital-efficient, asset-light model
QAAUM of Rs 9.69 lakh crore, up 10% YoY, with a leading 12.7% share of actively managed equity AUM
Record SIP inflows of Rs 32,500 crore in September 2026, pointing to durable, granular retail flows
First-ever 1:1 bonus issue (Nov 2025) alongside a rising dividend - TTM payout of Rs 54/share versus Rs 45 a year earlier
watchpoints: Headline PAT growth of just 4.2% YoY masks a 26% YoY drop in non-core 'other income'; watch whether core operating profit (up 16% YoY) remains the better guide or whether fee growth itself slows
Stock has badly lagged peer NAM-INDIA over 1, 3 and 5 years (-15.5% vs +22.6% over 1Y; +75% vs +200% over 3Y), suggesting the market sees slower relative growth ahead
Valuation is rich versus peers and industry - P/B near 10x versus a peer median of ~6.9x - even though it is below HDFC AMC's own historical average
AUM and fees are exposed to equity market cycles and to regulatory risk around mutual fund expense ratios, which is a periodic industry-wide threat
analysis.one_thing: Next quarter's split between core operating profit growth and 'other income' swings - if core fee-based profit keeps growing in the mid-teens while other income normalizes, the 4% headline this quarter was noise, not a trend.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 PAT of Rs 749 crore, the 4.2% YoY growth, QAAUM of Rs 9.69 lakh crore, and the other-income decline were cross-checked across Business Standard, Scanx, Equitybulls and aggregator sources. The company's own investor presentation PDF could not be fetched (paywalled/blocked), so figures rely on secondary reporting. Valuation ratios (P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE) and shareholding percentages are from third-party trackers (GuruFocus, Trendlyne, Anand Rathi), not pulled directly from the exchange filing; minor discrepancies between sources (e.g., P/E quoted as 32.9x-34x) were resolved by taking the cluster of similar values and discarding single outliers. Older Q2 results from 2023/2024 appeared in search results and were explicitly discarded in favor of the October 2026-dated FY27 figures.
